description: Detects when Up token bid-ask spread widens beyond rolling 20-snapshot median, then measures asymmetric depth recovery across top 3 book levels. Buy the token whose side market makers are replenishing faster.
hypothesis: When spread widens (liquidity withdrawal), the side where depth recovers first indicates which token market makers are re-quoting toward fair value, predicting resolution direction.

key_findings: Signal-triggered markets resolve Down 75% of the time — spread-widening filter selects markets where Up mid-price is low (mean 0.27), meaning market consensus already favors Down
Depth recovery signal adds no edge over naive always-buy-Down baseline (36.3% WR vs 75% Down base rate in selected markets)
Signal strength shows no meaningful separation between wins and losses (wins mean=-1259, losses mean=4158, massive variance)
All 7 parameter sweep configurations produce negative PnL; inverting signal direction is even worse
Strategy WR (36.3%) is worse than random coin flip (50.6%)
root_causes: 60-second observation window captures market-opening noise, not informative liquidity withdrawal/recovery cycles
Spread widening in early snapshots reflects initial market-making setup, not temporary liquidity retreat
Asymmetric depth recovery correlates with price level (low Up-price tokens have different depth profiles) rather than resolution direction

next_steps: Strategy requires full market-lifetime data (not just first 60s) to properly test spread mean-reversion hypothesis. The 60s sample captures opening dynamics where spreads are naturally wide and unstable, not the mid-market liquidity withdrawal events the hypothesis targets. Consider: (1) full parquet dataset across entire market lifetimes, (2) conditioning on time-within-market (e.g., final 2 minutes only), (3) controlling for mid-price level to avoid price-level confound.
